Visit note | 2025-03-31 11:30 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Shahana Mondal, 70, female. Mrs. Mondal attends today reporting no active symptoms, but she is concerned because her father suffered a heart attack at the age of 55. She works as a shopkeeper in Dhanmondi, where testing was prompted after a relative's heart attack. She has a known history of Hypothyroidism. She reports no chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.8 mmol/L, BP 118/81 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 70 kg. Her heart sounds are dual with no murmurs, and her lungs are clear. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-03-31 11:30 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Popy Miah, 67, female. Mrs. Miah presents with coughing at night, chest tightness when exposed to dust or cold air, and audible wheezing. She works as a farmer, and her symptoms have worsened since construction dust started near her home in Tejgaon. She has no significant past medical co-morbidities. She denies fever or recent weight loss. On examination: SpO2 95%, BP 118/81 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 45 kg. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-03-31 11:30 AM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Zahid Alam, 55, male. Mr. Alam complains of night pain in his shoulder, being unable to reach behind his back, and being unable to raise his arm properly. He works as a cricket coach in Kamrangirchar, and his trouble started after weeks of keeping his arm still following a sprain. He has no other chronic illnesses. He denies any neck pain or neurological deficits. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 90 degrees with restriction in all directions, BP 118/78 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 61 kg. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-03-31 11:30 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Tamim Faruque, 25, male. Mr. Faruque attends for a follow-up visit regarding his chronic nasal symptoms, noting that his sneezing and discomfort are worse with dust, accompanied by itchy eyes and a runny nose. He works as a sales representative in Tongi, and notes his condition has been worse since road construction began nearby. He has a known history of Essential hypertension. He reports no fever or facial pain. On examination: about 15 sneezing fits a day, BP 150/86 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 93 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-03-31 12:00 PM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Abdul Sikder, 46, male. Mr. Sikder presents today for his first visit, describing a tight chest when exposed to dust or cold air, along with troublesome wheezing and persistent coughing at night. He works as a farmer in Tangail, and reports that his respiratory symptoms flared up during the winter smog. He has no reported co-morbidities. He denies any history of cardiac disease or tuberculosis, though he admits to occasional casual smoking years ago. On examination, his oxygen saturation is notably reduced with SpO2 at 92 percent on room air. Other vitals show a blood pressure of 118/83 mmHg, a pulse rate of 91 beats per minute, and a body weight of 89 kg. Chest examination reveals diffuse expiratory wheezing across all lung zones with prolonged expiration, though breath sounds are vesicular and equal bilaterally. Cardiovascular examination reveals normal S1 and S2 heart sounds with no added murmurs or gallops. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued for bronchodilator therapy and controller medications. He was counselled extensively on avoiding dust and smoke, keeping his domestic sleeping quarters well aired at all times, and mastering the correct metered-dose inhaler technique. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 month to re-evaluate his symptom control and check his inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-04-02 10:00 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Habiba Matubbar, 22, female.
